title: Game On: More Than Just Fun!
topic_description: Recent reports highlight a concerning decline in physical activity among Hong Kong youth. Sedentary lifestyles, coupled with increasing academic pressure, are contributing to rising rates of obesity, stress, and mental health issues. Many schools are considering reducing time allocated to sports and physical education to focus on core academic subjects. However, advocates argue that this is a short-sighted approach, emphasizing the vital role sports play in holistic development. Consider this excerpt from a recent editorial: 'While academic achievement is undoubtedly important, neglecting physical well-being can have long-term detrimental effects. Sports offer a unique blend of physical, mental, and social benefits that are crucial for a well-rounded individual. Prioritizing a balance between academics and sports is essential for nurturing healthy, resilient, and successful young people.' Your school principal has asked for your opinions on the benefits of sports for students. Discuss the following aspects and come to a consensus on how to best promote sports within the school environment.
discussion_points: Benefits of sports for physical health and well-being.
The impact of sports on mental health and stress reduction.
Ways sports participation can improve social skills and teamwork.
How to increase sports participation in schools with demanding academic schedules.
individual_response_questions: What is your favourite sport and why?
Do you think schools should make sports compulsory? Why or why not?

candidates.A: Enthusiastic about sports and believes they are essential for overall well-being; focuses on personal experiences and positive outcomes.
candidates.B: Concerned about the time commitment and potential for injuries; questions whether the benefits of sports outweigh the risks and academic sacrifices.
candidates.C: Interested in practical solutions for incorporating sports into the school curriculum; focuses on logistical challenges, resource allocation, and student engagement strategies.
